title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive in an automated identification system, and it happened at the handoff between the alert and the officer in the field. A license plate reader misread the first letter of a plate and matched a BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The alert was then treated as a reason to stop a person at gunpoint, which is where a data error became a use of force.

Catching it would have required an independent check of the plate read before officers acted, which is the step Flock itself says should happen. The system produced a candidate match, and nothing between that match and the armed stop confirmed it. A misread of a single character is the kind of error a second look at the plate, or at the vehicle, is meant to surface.

What is not established is why the reader misread the plate. The sheriff's office attributed it to an illegal tinted plate cover and described the deputy's actions as reasonable, and those are the department's accounts rather than independent findings.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was reportedly held at gunpoint for more than five minutes after a Flock Safety license plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said such alerts should be checked independently before officers act.
title_en: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover
